A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MaskGCT. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original zero-shot TTS evaluations, subjective assessments, ablations and hard-case experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds original accent/emotion imitation, multilingual TTS and duration-constrained dubbing results.

M1.justification: The semantic VQ-VAE, masked T2S/S2A models, acoustic codec, losses, duration predictor and generation procedures remain unchanged. Retraining T2S on additional languages extends training coverage without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 adds Japanese, Korean, German and French training/evaluation and expands dubbing to 30 language directions (Appendices E–F). Section 4.3 adds L2-ARCTIC accent imitation and prompt-based emotion imitation on ESD; the latter differs from the emotion-label fine-tuning already present in v1.

E2.justification: The original TTS and AR + SoundStorm comparisons retain their comparator sets. V2 introduces Emilia-AR and Emilia-NAR alongside XTTS-v2 in the multilingual comparison (Table 11). NaturalSpeech 2 appears in the new descriptive capability table, not as a newly evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New style evaluations introduce CommonAccent/emotion2vec similarities and accent/emotion SMOS. Appendix E specifies T2S-only multilingual retraining and Whisper-medium WER evaluation. Appendix F introduces 200 source samples per language, GPT4o-mini translations and generation constrained to the source duration. The original benchmark protocols are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a phonetic-discriminability diagnostic, reporting ABX error below 5 for W2v-BERT 2.0 features versus above 20 for EnCodec features. Existing duration, inference-step, model-size, tokenizer and hard-case analyses remain; several are relocated to the appendices.

E5.justification: V1 reports subjective scores as point estimates; v2 systematically adds ± uncertainty terms to the retained SMOS/CMOS comparisons in Tables 2–3 and to the new style evaluations. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, although the terms' statistical meaning, confidence level and estimation procedure are unspecified. Additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: V2 adds style-imitation, four-language TTS, 30-direction dubbing and ABX results. Among retained results, T2S-Large English WER changes from 0.466 to 2.466 (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 6). MaskGCT's English/Chinese CMOS in the AR comparison changes from 0/0 to 0.03/0.05. The main objective TTS scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The masking formulation, codec losses, sampling expressions, duration-model equations and guidance formulas are retained. Appendix B's semantic/acoustic terminology discussion adds conceptual clarification, not new formal definitions, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces 'superior or competitive' performance with 'outperforms' and removes its explicit efficiency comparison against diffusion-based and autoregressive systems. V2 also explicitly emphasizes avoiding phone-level duration prediction. The principal two-stage TTS, duration-control and broader application contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix B qualifies semantic/acoustic terminology as non-rigorous. Appendix F adds language-dependent dubbing limitations and hypotheses involving duration constraints and limited French/German training data. Appendix E discusses the implications of retraining only T2S. The earlier speech-editing robustness limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 documents additional-language data amounts, T2S-only retraining, translation preparation and access to style-feature models. Core implementation details remain. Some existing documentation is lost: Figure 3 no longer specifies 25 T2S steps, and the relocated tokenizer table no longer explicitly states ground-truth duration.

R1.justification: V2 adds a capability-positioning table and references supporting style evaluation and semantic-token terminology, including L2-ARCTIC, emotion2vec, AudioLM, FireRedTTS and SpeechTokenizer. The HiFi-Codec reference is removed. The main related-work and concurrent-work arguments remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the document: method components become reordered subsections of Section 3.2, implementation appendices are consolidated under Appendix A, and detailed ablation material moves out of the main text. The abstract and introduction are rewritten, contributions are condensed, and citations switch to numerical form.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 2 and 5 are redrawn. V2 adds a capability table and four experimental tables, reformats subjective-score displays, wraps Figure 3 beside prose, and relocates Figure 4 and the tokenizer table to the appendices. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for MaskGCT's broad applicability. V1's bilingual benchmarks and demo-only translation discussion gain comparative style tests, four additional language evaluations and quantitative dubbing results that reveal failure conditions. Numerical corrections also improve internal consistency. Undefined uncertainty terms and lost caption settings limit reproducibility, but the new evidence and explicit applicability boundaries provide a substantial net quality gain.
